note: v1: TWO FLOORS, tribal / percussive warehouse techno where one bar holds two tempos. A 12-step pivot grid (triplet eighths) carries a shekere on every step, congas and an agogo line; under the MACHINE's floor (a 909 four-on-the-floor, steps 0 3 6 9) those twelve steps are a tribal shuffle at 128, under the TRIBE's floor (deep driven toms, three to the bar on 0 4 8) they are straight sixteenths at 96, and nothing about the tempo or the bar changes. The form walks between them: the groove in four (clap, open hats, a rolling G-minor bass galloping between the kicks, a Gm9 stab through a comb already sitting on the three-floor's off-beats); BOTH floors at once (4 against 3, the ear can stand on either); the 909 leaves and the bar SLOWS to 96 (clap, rim and hats move to the three); the break with no floor at all, the shekere's accents flipping between 4 and 3 every two bars over a drone and a Shepard riser (a Necker cube for tempo); then the drop: the four slamming back, with a distorted 909 layer, on top of the three. Mixed against the album: the first render was +8 to +18 dB heavy at 32-155 Hz (rumble and sub), cut; a hot master with parallel saturation and the set's dynamics after it (rms -12.9, crest 9.1). Seeds 0/11: 95.64 / 95.44 (variety 79 is the weak term: the limiter keeps the section range near 8 dB).
next: Widen the dynamics (variety 79): a real drop-out before the drop, or the slow section stripped to toms and shekere; give the tribe's floor more weight (a chest-hit tom kick); a hypnotic mutation in the long groove.

note: v2: the TRIBE GETS ITS CHEST and the set gets its contrast. Each of the toms' three-to-the-bar hits now has an 808 boom under it at the same pitch (D2 D2 A1), driven, so the tribe's floor hits as hard as the machine's, and the sustained 808 sub steps aside wherever the toms play (the boom is the low end there; the spectrum held at 95.3). The break got emptier: after the four drone bars the shekere plays ONLY its accents, four or three hits a bar, still flipping between the floors every two bars, so the Necker cube is bare bones, and bar 96 is a BLACKOUT, nothing but the riser's tail: the floor vanishes, then the four slams back over the three. And the slow section opens bare (toms, boom, shekere and the three-floor backbeat; the rolling bass re-enters at bar 69), so the slowing lands as a reveal. Seeds 0/11 (pin 3c2c411f; v1 byte-identical): 95.642 / 95.436 -> 97.579 / 97.325, variety 79 -> 90 (density cv .10 -> .15).
next: Harry's notes; a hypnotic mutation through the long groove (the stab's filter or the conga line evolving); maybe a formant-pitched vocal chop (wM's new pitch.formant) on the three-floor; widen the level range (still ~8 dB).

note: v3: the TRIBE SHOUTS and the stab OPENS. A short, dark vocal hit now lands on the three-floor's third beat: a song-local chant voice (saw, pulse and breath through a formant filter on 'ah', each throat a little different), made bigger and darker with wM's new formant-preserving pitch (same note, formants down 4: a larger throat, not a slower one), driven and pumping, a shout on D4 and its answer on G3: every other bar once the toms are in, every bar on the slow floor and through the drop, so the tribe's floor has a voice the 909's does not. And the hypnotic mutation: the Gm9 stab's low-pass climbs from 500 Hz to 5 kHz through the long groove and again through the drop, dark in between, the same loop slowly brightening. Re-measured like for like: v2 now scores 95.141 / 94.895 since t3 exists (a new flow term: the join from The One Comes Home is 18.9 dB level and 24 dB spectral, my intro's 909 sub straight after t3's bright end); v3 95.286 / 95.432, spectrum 95.3 -> 96.5. The chant sits ~6.6 dB under the slow section's mix. motifs.md: THE STAB opens, THE TRIBE SHOUTS.
next: Fix the join from t3: open on the highs (shekere, hats) and bring the 909 in under them, or fade in; Harry's notes.

note: v4, answering Harry (4/10: too busy, needs better taste, all comes in too fast n heavy): RESTRAINT AND PATIENCE. Removed the congas, the agogo line and the drop's distorted kick layer; the chant now shouts every other bar. Every part now earns its entrance: the shekere's shuffle ALONE for four bars (the pivot, the one sound both tempos share), the hats at 5, the 909 and its rumble at 9, the sub at 13, the rolling bass at 17, the clap at 21, the stab not until 33; the tribe still arrives over four bars at 49. And the movement now comes from slow LFOs on odd lengths instead of more layers: the stab's filter on a 5-bar cycle and its resonance on a 7-bar one (against the 4-bar phrases it never repeats quite the same), the rolling bass's filter breathing on 3 bars, the shekere drifting across the field over 7. Re-measured like for like (Harry's 4 now counts): v3 78.009 / 78.110 -> v4 79.699 / 79.708; variety 90 -> 100 (section range 8 -> 13.8 dB: emptier is louder by contrast), and the quiet, high opening halves the join from t3 (level jump 18.9 -> 10.8 dB, spectral 24 -> 13.6). motifs.md updated.
next: Harry's next notes; keep refining, not adding: the drop's weight and clarity (kick vs boom vs bass), the reveal timing of the slow floor, maybe trim the chant further.

note: v5 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail), still answering 'all comes in too fast n heavy': the DROP is now as patient as the opening. Before, everything came back at bar 97 at once (both floors, clap, hats, bass, stab, chant). Now the drop lands on the illusion alone, bare and heavy: the 909's four and the toms' three with their booms, the shekere pivot and the rolling bass, nothing else for four bars, so you hear the two tempos fighting with nothing to hide behind; the hats return at 101, the clap at 105, and the stab (its filter on the 5-bar LFO) and the chant wait until 113 for the last sixteen bars of the peak. Seeds 0/11 (pin 8bdbbd47; v4 byte-identical, re-measured 86.699 / 86.700): 86.670 / 86.671. motifs.md: the drop lands bare.

note: v6 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail): THE LOW END INTERLOCKS, still answering 'too heavy'. Where both floors play (the 'both' section and the drop) three low sources were piling onto the same steps: the 909 and the toms' 808 boom both on the one, and the rolling bass's gallop landing on the booms at steps 4 and 8. Now each low hit has its own step: the 909 owns the one alone (the tom still strikes there, without its boom), and the bass plays only the gaps between both floors' hits (steps 1 2 5 7 10 11 instead of eight), so the gallop has air in it and the low end reads as an interlock of three parts rather than a pile. The rumble bus's sends are also 6 dB lower (less wash: master rms -13.0 -> -13.5, crest 9.1 -> 9.5). Measured honestly: the low band's crest barely moves (6.5 -> 6.1 dB), the master's limiting sets it, so this is a cleaner arrangement more than a meter change. Seeds 0/11 (pin a1769d62; v5 byte-identical at 86.670 / 86.671): 86.674 / see note. motifs.md: the interlock.

note: v7 (judgment keep; level on the guardrail): THE REVEAL GETS ITS MOMENT (Harry's polish list: the timing of each illusion's reveal). The slow floor used to arrive by subtraction alone, the 909 just stopping at bar 65 while the toms carried on, easy to miss as a change of tempo. Now bar 64 is a PIVOT BAR: everything stops except the shekere, and its accents have already moved onto the three (0 4 8), so for one bar the only thing telling the ear the tempo is the pivot itself, saying three; then the toms land on it at 65 and the same bar is 96. One bar, nothing added. Seeds 0/11 (pin b93526ee; v6 byte-identical, 86.676 / 86.675): 86.680 / 86.685; compscore now hears the pivot as its own event (sections 7 -> 8). motifs.md.
